blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements released per Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) App Connector version.

This App Connector software version includes an update for reporting application health. In order to prevent App Connector performance degradation during application discovery, App Connectors perform application reachability checks for a maximum of 6000 applications for Application Segments configured with Health Reporting set to On Access.
There is no limit to the number of applications that an App Connector is capable of monitoring for Application Segments configured for Health Reporting set to Continuous.
Your App Connectors will be updated based on your software update schedule as configured per App Connector group. To learn more, see About App Connector Software Updates.
This App Connector software version includes updates that:

blocks.item: Enable Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Log Streaming Service (LSS) to encrypt logs between the LSS App Connector and a log receiver using TLS encryption.

Allow the software to reuse open UDP sockets for initiating connections to application servers instead of opening a new UDP socket for an application connection. This change reduces the number of UDP ports that are used by an App Connector to open connections to application servers, which reduces the possibility of UDP port exhaustion on the App Connector host.
Address an issue where the App Connector software experienced degradation when processing traffic for applications over UDP.

blocks.item: For an App Connector that is explicitly configured to send traffic to a proxy, you can configure the App Connector to bypass the proxy for traffic that needs to be sent to specific destinations.

This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:

blocks.item: The amount of available memory for App Connectors is now calculated as the sum of free memory and any cached memory for the system.
The App Connector logs now show the App Connector uptime as a readable string with the format: "X days Y hours Z seconds".
The App Connector will log the CPU, memory, and disk utility stats in the App Connector status logs.
A fix was released to correctly display the number of file descriptors in the App Connector logs.

blocks.item: Additional timestamps were added to User Activity Logs and to messages used for communication between the Service Edge, Central Authority, and App Connector components of the ZPA cloud.

This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:

blocks.item: Enable Zscaler Private Access (ZPA) Public Service Edges (formerly Zscaler Enforcement Nodes or ZENs) to redirect an App Connector's control connection to the geographically closest Public Service Edge. This is based on the load for ZPA Public Service Edges and the App Connector's geolocation.
This release contains software updates to support the new ZPA Private Service Edge functionality. To learn more, see About ZPA Private Service Edges.
A fix was released to resolve an issue where the App Connector would crash if the App Connector process was started after creating a tunnel interface.
A fix was released to address an issue where an App Connector would experience service degradation when it could not identify a Mac address of a tunnel interface.
A fix was released to reduce the log volume of connection status logs during the normal course of an App Connector’s operation.
There are new OVA and RPM packages for version 2020.06 available for deploying App Connectors.
Starting with OVA version 2020.06, rsyslogd is disabled for App Connectors.
A fix was released to address an App Connector software degradation issue that occurred when the App Connector was processing traffic for applications enabled for double encryption.

This App Connector software version includes the following improvements:

blocks.item: Resolved an issue where some App Connectors that upgraded from version 19.102.3 to 20.11.13 experienced performance degradation when processing updates from another microservice or when resolving nested DNS CNAME records.

To reduce the volume of DNS traffic that App Connectors and different ZPA microservices process, ZPA Central Authority (CA) will only send DNS requests to a maximum of two available App Connectors within a App Connector group during the application discovery process.

App Connectors will no longer send application availability messages to the ZPA CA when Application Segments are configured with Health Reporting set to On Access and Health Check set to Disabled. This change means:
The ZPA CA will assume the application is reachable through the App Connectors.
There is a reduction in the volume of application availability messages sent by App Connectors and processed by the ZPA CA.
The process for selecting a connector for a requested application is faster.
Additional fields have been added to the App Connector Status logs for visibility and troubleshooting.
App Connectors will automatically restart if the available disk space is less than 100 MB.

This App Connector software version includes an enhancement to reduce the duration for which App Connectors consume a UDP socket, so that UDP sockets are used more efficiently. If the App Connector is requesting applications on UDP ports 88, 123, 161, or 389, the App Connector will release the UDP socket after 2 seconds from the instance it started consuming the socket. For access on all other UDP ports, the App Connector will continue to hold onto UDP socket for 60 seconds.
